what_its_for: Vorinostat is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of skin cancer called cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL). It is used when the cancer has come back or gotten worse after other treatments. It works by blocking certain proteins in cancer cells that help them grow, which slows down or stops the cancer from spreading.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Do NOT open, crush, or chew the capsule. Take it with food to help reduce nausea and upset stomach. Try to take it at the same time each day. If the powder inside the capsule touches your skin or eyes by accident, wash the area right away with plenty of water.
dosing: The usual dose is 400 mg (two 200 mg capsules) taken by mouth once a day. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store vorinostat capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed and away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a safe drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink plenty of water and fluids every day, especially if you have diarrhea or vomiting. Avoid taking aspirin or blood thinners (like warfarin) without talking to your doctor first, as vorinostat can increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid live vaccines while on this medicine. Tell your doctor before taking any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements. Avoid pregnancy — this medicine can harm an unborn baby, so use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of a blood clot such as leg pain, swelling, or redness; shortness of breath or chest pain; signs of dehydration such as extreme thirst, dry mouth, or not urinating; unusual bleeding or bruising; fast or irregular heartbeat; severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that won't stop; signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst and frequent urination; or any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: Vorinostat does not cure CTCL, but it can help slow the growth of cancer and improve your symptoms. Some patients begin to see improvement within the first few weeks to months of treatment, but it may take longer. Your doctor will monitor how well the medicine is working with regular check-ups and tests.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if you are pregnant. Women who could become pregnant and male patients with female partners who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects such as dehydration and should drink extra fluids. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or your doctor may monitor you more closely.
